hook.1: One month is a chain: money comes in, and every choice changes what is left for the next.
hook.2: Cover needs and commitments first, then save. A projection is an assumption, not a promise.
hook.3: You will budget, check a payment, compare borrowing and read a savings range — all connected.

lesson.title: One month, connected choices
lesson.priorityLabel: Income has arrived. What do you fund first?
lesson.projectionLabel: A plan shows a savings amount in 3 years. What is that figure?
lesson.assumption: An assumption based on the stated rates
lesson.promise: A promise that the money will be there

budget.title: Budget the month
budget.prompt: Fictional Nikhil's month: income has arrived. Cover rent, food and the ₹4,500 instalment first, save something, and place every rupee in a jar.
budget.hint1: Fund rent, food and the instalment before wants, then save something.
budget.hint2: Place every rupee; an unallocated pool is not a plan.
budget.explanation: Needs and the existing instalment come first, then savings; wants come after. Every rupee placed means nothing is forgotten.

no_essentials.review: Your choice: left rent, food or the existing instalment unfunded. Safer choice: cover needs and commitments before wants. Concept: essentials and the instalment come first in a monthly plan. Why it matters: missing them creates arrears and extra charges.

no_savings.review: Your choice: placed every rupee but saved nothing. Safer choice: keep a small saving after needs and commitments. Concept: paying yourself first builds a cushion. Why it matters: without savings, the next surprise becomes debt.

upi.title: Check before you pay
upi.prompt: A message says an unpaid bill must be paid today to an unfamiliar account. The name and handle were not verified. What do you do?
upi.hint1: A payment you authorise sends your money. Check the full recipient details first.
upi.hint2: Urgency is a warning sign. Never enter a PIN for a handle you have not verified.
upi.pay: Enter the mock PIN and pay now
upi.decline: Decline and verify the name and handle first
upi.explanation: Paying an unverified handle risks sending money to the wrong person with little chance of recovery. Verifying the recipient first is the safer choice.

wrong_payee.review: Your choice: paid an unverified payee under time pressure. Safer choice: confirm the exact name and handle before authorising. Concept: a payment moves your money once you authorise it. Why it matters: money sent to the wrong payee is hard to recover.

loan.title: Compare two fictional loans
loan.prompt: Fictional Nikhil needs a ₹40,000 loan and can repay within a year. Two fictional offers share the same 12% rate and ₹400 fee: 12 months or 36 months. Both instalments fit the ₹10,000 left each month. Which option repays less overall?
loan.hint1: A smaller EMI can last longer and add more interest. Compare the total repaid, not only the monthly figure.
loan.hint2: Read the fees and total repayment on each fictional card before choosing.
loan.twelveAssumptions: Assumption: a fictional loan at 12% a year with a ₹400 fee; EMI, interest and total are model figures, not an offer.
loan.thirtySixAssumptions: Assumption: the same fictional loan over 36 months at 12% a year with a ₹400 fee; EMI, interest and total are model figures, not an offer.
loan.explanation: The 36-month option lowers each instalment but raises interest and the total repaid. The 12-month option costs less overall here; a shorter term is only suitable if the instalment stays manageable.

ignored_total_cost.review: Your choice: picked the longer loan for its lower monthly instalment. Safer choice: compare total repayment and fees, not only the EMI. Concept: a longer tenure can raise total interest and cost. Why it matters: more of next months' income is committed for longer.

savings.title: A range is not a promise
savings.prompt: Fictional Nikhil sets aside ₹5,000 for up to 3 years. The illustration assumes a 6% annual rate with a 2 percentage-point spread and 4% inflation. What does the range show?
savings.hint1: A range built from assumptions is an illustration, not a minimum or a promise.
savings.hint2: Choose the answer that treats the higher and lower lines as model endpoints.
savings.promise: The graph guarantees my money reaches at least the lower line.
savings.assumption: It is an assumed illustration; neither the growth nor the lower line is guaranteed.
savings.explanation: The lines come from assumed rates, not a forecast. A real result can be lower, including a loss.

guaranteed_return.review: Your choice: treated an assumed projection as a promise. Safer choice: read the assumptions and keep the possibility of loss. Concept: a projection is not a guarantee. Why it matters: a plan that assumes a floor can leave a goal unfunded.

decision.title: One connected month
decision.prompt: This month is one chain: budget the income, check a payment before you pay, compare a borrowing option, and read a savings figure honestly. Every person and number here is fictional; nothing is a recommendation.
decision.hint1: Work left to right: fund needs and the instalment, then verify, compare, and question the number.
decision.hint2: Each link feeds the next. A weak choice earlier changes what is left later.
decision.explanation: The chain holds only when every link holds: needs and commitments covered, the payment checked, the loan cost examined, and the savings figure read as an assumption. A weak link weakens the month.

consequence.month: Assumption, not a forecast: in this fictional month, income is ₹30,000. Rent and essentials plus the existing ₹4,500 instalment need ₹16,500, leaving the rest to save. The chosen 12-month loan has an EMI of ₹3,553.95 and a total repayment of ₹43,047.43. A ₹5,000 savings illustration for 3 years at assumed rates of 4% and 8% shows ₹5,624.32 to ₹6,298.56 before fees and taxes; a real result can be lower, including a loss.
consequence.next: Cover needs and the instalment, verify the payee, compare the whole loan cost, and treat the savings range as an assumption — and the month holds together.
consequence.explanation: No single number decides a month. Budgeting, checking a payment, reading the full loan cost and treating savings honestly fit together; a mistake in one link changes what is left for the next.

transfer.hint1: Read the whole month: the fraud attempt changes what you do with the money.
transfer.hint2: Stop and check any message that rushes you or asks for a code or a click.

meera.title: A different month: Meera
meera.prompt: Fictional Meera's month runs the same chain — budget, a message, borrowing, saving — but a fraud attempt is in the middle.
meera.budget: Fictional Meera's month: place her income so needs, the ₹4,500 instalment and savings are all covered.
meera.loan: Fictional Meera needs a ₹30,000 loan. Which of these two offers costs less overall?
meera.savings: Fictional Meera sets aside ₹5,000 for 3 years. What does the assumed range show?
meera.explanation: Meera keeps the month whole by covering needs, refusing the OTP request, choosing the lower total cost, and treating the savings range as an assumption.

arjun.title: A different month: Arjun
arjun.prompt: Fictional Arjun's month chains budget, borrowing, a message and saving, with a fraud attempt in the middle.
arjun.budget: Fictional Arjun's month: fund needs and the ₹4,500 instalment, keep a saving, and assign every rupee.
arjun.loan: Fictional Arjun needs a ₹50,000 loan. Which of these two offers costs less overall?
arjun.savings: Fictional Arjun sets aside ₹5,000 for 3 years. What does the assumed range show?
arjun.explanation: Arjun keeps the month whole by funding needs first, comparing the whole loan cost, refusing the prize link, and treating the savings range as an assumption.

fraud.title: A message in the month
fraud.prompt: Classify this fictional message and select every warning sign it shows.
fraud.hint1: Real institutions do not ask for a code, a PIN or a click through an urgent message.
fraud.hint2: Name the warning signs: urgency, a request for a secret code, an unknown sender, a prize or a link.
fraud.explanation: The message is fraud: it uses urgency and asks for a secret code or a link. Stop, do not reply or click, and report it through an official channel.
fraud.otpSender: Unknown number (claims to be a bank desk)
fraud.otpBody: Your account will be frozen in 30 minutes. Reply now with the 6-digit code we sent to stop it.
fraud.linkBody: Congratulations, you won a prize! Tap this link and enter your details before the offer ends today.

sign.asksOtp: Asks for a secret code or OTP
sign.link: Asks you to tap a link
sign.prize: Promises a prize you did not enter for

shared_otp.review: Your choice: treated a code request as safe. Safer choice: never share an OTP; a real institution will not ask for it. Concept: a shared code can authorise fraud. Why it matters: money can leave your account.

clicked_link.review: Your choice: trusted a prize link. Safer choice: do not click links in unexpected messages. Concept: links can lead to phishing. Why it matters: details or money can be stolen.
